claims.text: Machine-learning-based potentials can describe the structure of high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states.
EAM references are unable to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid.
A machine-learning-based potential can overcome the limitations of EAM references.
Using a machine-learning-based potential improves representation of the relevant atomic configurations.
Improved representation of atomic configurations produces better reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learning reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys at and near their high melting temperatures.
TOR-TILD's EAM references provide the comparison baseline.
The effectiveness of the machine-learning potential for improving phase-space overlap and reducing path mismatch remains uncertain and requires testing.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing machine-learning and EAM references using phase-space overlap and thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Failure to obtain a significant improvement in both phase-space overlap and path mismatch would falsify the hypothesis.
